thread:
alex: Heads up — prod GPU edge hosts in eu-west are intermittently failing DNS for our internal model registry (model-registry.internal). Pods try to fetch weights and timeout, causing scale-ups to stall. :eyes:
chloe: Can you paste the logs / a repro? is this only eu-west?
alex: Repro on staging too. Quick log snippet:```2026-03-15T09:12:03Z model-fetcher[pid=1245] ERR lookup model-registry.internal: NXDOMAIN; fallback to s3 -> delay 12s```
devon: Did you check /etc/resolv.conf on the node and inside the pod? we had similar where CNI rewrote to a local stub.
alex: node /etc/resolv.conf shows:```nameserver 127.0.0.53#53
options ndots:5
search eu-west.internal svc.cluster.local cluster.local``` inside pod it's the same (ClusterFirst).
maria: Hmm our edge CNI started injecting a local dnsmasq stub last week to reduce query egress. It seems fine normally but might be dropping or returning SERVFAIL for split-horizon internal names when under load. :thinking:
devon: Also saw the inference runtime keeps a mmap-backed hostcache for model-registry lookups (was added to speed repeated model resolves). That cache doesn't respect negative TTLs from the stub — restarting the process clears it immediately. Could explain intermittent after a bad NX.
alex: We rolled a restart of the GPU model-fetchers in the eu-west pool and errors cleared for ~20m, then resurfaced on new nodes.
chloe: Any difference in NAT/egress for those nodes? port rotation / conntrack could affect responses if requests are proxied to a remote forwarder.
maria: Network team confirms we route DNS from eu-west edge pool to a central forwarder in the same region via NAT gateway, but sticky SNAT was recently disabled for the auto-scale groups -> ephemeral source ports now.
devon: If the forwarder uses a short negative cache and the stub returns NX then the mmap cache will keep it. We should either honor negative TTL better or bypass the local stub for split-horizon domains.
sre-oncall: Noted incident. Quick mitigation: pin egress for edge GPU subnet to the regional forwarder with source-affinity and roll dnsmasq config to increase negative-ttl to 30s. I'll open the policy.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-032-118 — "edge eu-west DNS nx/cache flapping impacting model fetch" (severity: P2). Link: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-2026-032-118
chloe: For a short-term test in staging, try setting kubelet flag --cluster-dns to the forwarder IP instead of using the local stub, and disable the CNI stub. We can also lower ndots from 5 to 2 for the model-fetcher pods as a stopgap.
alex: Confirmed lowering ndots to 2 in staging reduced failures in my test.
devon: Longer term: 1) make mmap hostcache respect negative TTL / add eviction on NX, 2) add explicit hosts fallback in the init container for model-registry to avoid DNS on cold boot, 3) restore egress source-affinity on edge autoscale groups.
maria: I'll coordinate with netops for the egress affinity change and push a dnsmasq config with higher negative-ttl to the edge image.
chloe: I'll open a PR to change kubelet resolvConf behavior in our node config for staging and add an integration test that simulates stub failures.
sre-oncall: Assign actions: maria (egress affinity + dnsmasq patch), devon (hostcache patch + init-hosts), chloe (kubelet/resolvConf + test), alex (verify canary rolling for model-fetchers). ETA 48h for rollout to staging, then prod.
alex: Thanks — will monitor and post any new patterns. :thumbsup:
